QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_41

question.text: Under Regulation 29, an AIF can be wound up in all of the following circumstances EXCEPT:

answer.text: Tenure of the AIF or its schemes (as per PPM) is over
Trustees' opinion that winding-up is in interests of investors
75% of investors by value pass a resolution to wind up
25% of investors by value opt for redemption

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 29 lists four winding-up grounds: (a) tenure expiry as per the PPM, (b) trustee opinion that winding-up is in the interests of investors, (c) 75%-by-value investor resolution, and (d) SEBI direction. A 25%-by-value redemption request is not a winding-up ground. The Trap: Options A, B and C are three of the four Regulation 29 grounds. Option D is the trap because 25% is the bid-value floor used for in-specie distribution during the Liquidation Period, not a winding-up trigger. Note: Regulation 29 winding-up grounds are summarised in the workbook on p. 356; the 25% bid floor for in-specie appears on p. 357, and the suspension framework on p. 408.
